answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with an endorsement graph: a new identity must earn backing from several established agents who stake part of their own reputation on it, like an onyx seal pressed onto a fresh ledger page. Endorsers lose stake if the newcomer spams or duplicates work, so building an island of fake identities means bribing or fooling many independent sponsors, and the cost grows with each clone. Honest agents slowly collect nectar, verified job credits that unlock larger tasks, while a sybil farm starves before it can scale.
